title: Asset Handling Requirements
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 2: Asset Security: Asset Handling Requirements.

items: Media must be marked/labeled with its classification level
Handling procedures must match the classification of data on the media
Physical media requires secure storage appropriate to classification
Transporting classified media requires encryption or secure courier
Downgrading media classification requires sanitization first

blocks.text: Media handling encompasses the entire lifecycle:

items: Storage — Locked cabinets, safes, or controlled access rooms based on classification
Transport — Encryption for digital media; secure courier for physical
Disposal — Appropriate sanitization method based on classification
Reuse — Must be properly sanitized before reuse, especially at lower classification levels

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: Media containing classified data cannot simply be reformatted and reused for unclassified purposes. Proper sanitization (clearing, purging, or destruction) is required first.

items: Archives must maintain classification protections throughout retention period
Storage media should be tested periodically for reliability
Environmental controls (temperature, humidity) affect media longevity
Archive accessibility must be ensured for the entire retention period
Consider technology obsolescence when choosing archive media

blocks.text: From the Official CBK: Data archiving requirements include:

items: Media type selection
Security requirements maintenance
Availability requirements throughout retention
Media degradation — Magnetic media degrades over time; optical media can last longer
Format obsolescence — Can you still read this format in 20 years?
Hardware availability — Will compatible drives/readers exist?
Encryption key management — Archived encrypted data is useless without keys
